analysis.title: Commodity Views: 2027 Outlook: Adapting to Rough Waters
key_insights: GS recommends a positive commodities allocation. Its base case of further energy price moderation implies near-zero BCOM total returns through end-2027, after +26% YTD. Tactical and structural drivers still support the hedging and diversification value of commodities.
Base case 2027 average Brent is $88/bbl and European TTF gas is 45 EUR/MWh, as Mideast supply keeps adapting.

The November selloff in energy and copper reflects shifts in sentiment and near-term Mideast escalation risk, not physical fundamentals. GS estimates the Brent spot risk premium fell from $27 on the Friday before the midterms to a few dollars, which it sees as a more attractive entry point for hedges.
Recent tanker attacks near Hormuz and the difficulty of a lasting diplomatic breakthrough put downside risk on GS's base case for rising Persian Gulf commodity supply.

Energy prices ran well above prewar expectations in 2026 but rose less than GS and consensus expected given how long the Iran conflict has lasted. Demand adaptation (energy destocking, fuel switching especially in China) and supply adaptation explain the gap.

Persian Gulf crude exports recovered to near 2025 levels in September and the global oil market likely returned to surplus in October. GS expects ship-to-ship transfers and pipeline additions to lift Mideast oil output to an average 1.1mb/d above 2025 levels in 2027.

Supply adaptation has worked less well for refined products, LNG and aluminium feedstock. These are harder to transfer ship-to-ship (more flammable than crude), and refining, aluminium smelting and LNG liquefaction capacity is not fully repaired from strikes.

Tanker adaptation to Mideast shipping risk accounts for about 3/4 of the roughly $20/bbl y/y rise in the global average crude freight rate. GS expects freight to stay high while ship-to-ship transfers and the US blockade of Iran persist. Higher freight passes through to retail fuel prices.

Upside energy scenario: if 2027 Gulf output stays 2.5mb/d below 2025, Brent could exceed $130 in early 2027 and average about $120 in 2027. US wholesale diesel could reach a new high of $230 around year-end if refining output falls a further 3mb/d.

TTF could reach near 150 EUR/MWh in 2027Q1 if Gulf LNG exports run at 25-30% of pre-war levels this winter and the winter is 1 std. dev. colder. If Gulf LNG exports stall near 35% of pre-war levels through end-2027, TTF would average 104 EUR/MWh in 2027.
The GS TTF base case includes a subjective 30% probability of the low winter supply scenario, down from 45% because of a sharp month-to-date rise in Mideast LNG exports.

Equities and especially bonds have become unusually sensitive to energy prices since the war began. Daily Brent changes correlate strongly with S&P 500 and 10Y yield changes, though the 1-month correlation between Brent and the 10Y yield has turned negative since late September as AI and risk-asset volatility took over as the main driver.

A renewed energy supply shock in 2027 could mean lower bond prices (as in 2026) and lower equities (as in 2022), given GS's base case of slower earnings growth and downside risks to GDP and employment. Commodities would then diversify when it matters most.
Over the past six decades, in every 12-month period when both equities and bonds had negative real returns, either gold or broader commodities had positive real returns.

Agriculture: BCOM Agriculture is up 10% YTD with upside risk from the Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, a likely Super El Niño (forecast as the strongest on record) and possible food export restrictions. Hormuz-linked trade is typically 1/3 of global fertilizer exports, and the Black Sea is 15-20% of global grain trade.

El Niño crop risks: West Africa cocoa drought risk in 2026Q4, and Vietnam robusta coffee risk in 2027Q1 if groundwater and reservoir levels fall. Low European river levels (Danube, Rhine) are constraining shipping, irrigation and cooling.

Trade: long EBOB Jun27 European gasoline. Refiners are switching output to diesel and jet, and gasoline margins are low, leaving room for upside. GS cites a 20% total expected return in the base case and 62% under renewed escalation, and a 4% loss in the downside scenario.
Trade: long call spreads on TTF 2027Q1 to hedge a tight European winter, given low European inventories and the recent risk premium liquidation.

Copper: GS forecasts LME copper at $15,600/t by Dec27 (+13% from spot), driven by electrification, energy security, stockpiling, data centers and AI against constrained mine supply. US tariff ambiguity has pulled refined copper into US stockpiles, and China's tighter scrap-invoicing rules push semi-fabricators toward cathode. Ex-US stocks are at seasonal lows.

Near-term downside risks to the copper forecast are a reduction in US tariff ambiguity and a lackluster recovery in AI-related investor length. GS expects positioning to at least partly recover because the midterm results are more likely to delay than derail US data center growth.

Aluminium: GS expects an Indonesia supply boom (China-backed smelting) to push the market into surplus and cut the price to $2,600/t by Dec27. Indonesian primary output is forecast at about 4% of global by end-2027 versus 1% at end-2025. The long Dec27 copper / short Dec27 aluminium trade should be more resilient to macro-driven positioning cuts than outright long copper.

Gold: GS cuts its Dec27 forecast to $4,650/toz from $4,800, about 16% upside from spot. Economists now expect a second 25bp Fed hike in December 2026 and a third in March 2027. Central bank buying provides a floor, and private investor demand should return once the Fed starts easing in December 2027.
Long-dated gas trade: long puts on TTF Summer 2029, because the 2025-26 LNG FID wave adds to post-2027 supply and leaves longer-term balances oversupplied.

Structural case: geopolitical fragmentation colliding with concentrated commodity supply (2022 Russian gas shock, last year's Chinese rare earths shock, this year's Hormuz cross-commodity shock) has structurally raised disruption risk. A broad commodity basket excluding precious metals offers the most robust protection.

sector_views.rationale: Positive allocation as a hedge against supply shocks, with risk premia sharply lower and structural demand meeting constrained supply in copper and gold.
Base case is further price moderation (Brent $88 in 2027) with a Mideast supply recovery, but tail risk from renewed escalation and a cold winter justifies targeted hedges.
Copper rises to $15,600/t by Dec27 on electrification and AI demand against mine supply constraints, while aluminium falls to $2,600 on Indonesian supply.
Structural central bank buying, with a more difficult near-term setup due to Fed hikes and private demand returning once easing starts in December 2027.
Upside risk from conflicts, a Super El Niño and possible export restrictions, with BCOM Agriculture already up 10% YTD.

trade_ideas.description: Long BCOM (Bloomberg Commodity Index) as a supply-shock hedge for bond-equity portfolios
trade_ideas.rationale: Commodity supply is concentrated and disruption risk is high but unpredictable, so broad commodity exposure hedges supply shocks.

trade_ideas.description: Long EBOB Jun27 European gasoline futures
trade_ideas.rationale: Refiners switching output from gasoline to diesel tightens gasoline, and low margins leave room for sharp upside if the conflicts constrain refining or damage infrastructure.
trade_ideas.risk: In the downside scenario, with damaged refining capacity restored and Gulf supply beating base case by 1.4mb/d, the trade loses 4%.

trade_ideas.description: Long call spreads on TTF European natural gas 2027Q1
trade_ideas.rationale: Renewed escalation cutting LNG supply plus a colder-than-average winter could send European gas sharply higher, with inventories currently low.
A structural central bank bid provides a floor through the Fed hiking cycle, and easing from late 2027 should unlock private investor demand.
trade_ideas.risk: Fed hikes weigh on private investor positioning through early 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Long Dec-27 LME copper, short Dec-27 LME aluminium
trade_ideas.rationale: Copper faces mine supply constraints, electrification demand and low ex-US stocks, while China-backed smelting in Indonesia pushes aluminium into surplus.
trade_ideas.risk: Reduced US tariff ambiguity or a lackluster recovery in AI-related investor length could pressure copper.

trade_ideas.description: Long puts on TTF Summer 2029 (short 2029 European gas)
trade_ideas.rationale: Longer-term LNG balances look oversupplied as the 2025-26 LNG FID wave adds post-2027 supply.

risk_factors: Renewed Mideast escalation, such as stepped-up shipping attacks or damage to energy infrastructure, could spike energy prices and hit bonds and equities.
A cold European winter with low gas inventories and weak Gulf LNG exports.
Downside risk to the Persian Gulf supply base case from tanker attacks near Hormuz.
A Super El Niño, droughts, low European river levels and food export restrictions could lift agricultural prices.
Reduced US tariff ambiguity or a weak recovery in AI-related investor length could pressure copper.
A third Fed hike and a hawkish Fed outlook could pressure gold in the near term.
Downside scenario: Persian Gulf supply beating the base case by 1.4mb/d and refining capacity restored would cut gasoline trade returns.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots GS's Brent risk premium estimate, which dropped from $27 before the midterms to a few dollars.
Exhibit 6 shows 2027Q1 TTF scenarios: base case rising winter supply 65, low winter supply 102, 1 std. dev. colder 106 to 147 and 1 std. dev. warmer 41 to 58, against forwards of 85 EUR/MWh.
Exhibit 7 shows 6-month rolling correlation of Brent with S&P 500 and 10Y yields, while the 1-month Brent versus 10Y yield correlation has turned negative since late September.
Exhibit 17 lists GS price forecasts: Brent $93 now, $88 2027 average; copper $13,821 now, $15,400 2027 average, $15,600 Dec27; aluminium $3,085 now, $2,700 2027 average.
vol_and_positioning: Copper investor length has fallen on recent AI-related equity volatility. GS expects positioning to at least partly recover.
Private investor gold positioning is expected to stay subdued through early 2027 while the Fed hikes and recover once easing begins in December 2027.
The copper long / aluminium short trade is seen as less exposed to macro-driven positioning reductions (a turn in the AI cycle, more Fed hikes) than outright long copper.
GS favors asymmetric hedges: EBOB Jun27 gasoline futures and TTF 2027Q1 call spreads, entered after the recent risk premium liquidation.
The stock-bond correlation has risen over the past five to six years as supply shocks became more prominent and globalization stalled.
geopolitical: Iran conflict and US-Iran war: Persian Gulf export adaptation through ship-to-ship transfers and pipelines, with a US blockade of Iranian tankers.
Recent tanker attacks near Hormuz and the challenge of a lasting Mideast diplomatic breakthrough.
Russia-Ukraine conflict constraining refining output and Black Sea grain exports.
US-China competition for refined copper and for AI and power, with US tariff ambiguity and China's push for security of supply.
US midterms, which GS expects to delay rather than derail US data center capacity growth.
Geopolitical fragmentation: the 2022 Russian gas shock, last year's Chinese rare earths shock and this year's Hormuz shock.

tension_points.bull_case: Mideast supply keeps adapting. Persian Gulf crude exports are near 2025 levels, the oil market is likely in surplus, and Brent averages $88 in 2027 with TTF at 45 EUR/MWh.
tension_points.bear_case: Renewed escalation or damage to energy infrastructure could push Brent above $130 in early 2027, and a cold winter with low Gulf LNG could take TTF near 150 EUR/MWh in 2027Q1.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A base case invalidation would be 2027 average Gulf output staying 2.5mb/d below 2025, or Gulf LNG exports staying at 25-30% of pre-war levels through winter.

tension_points.bull_case: Structural central bank buying provides a floor, and private investor demand returns once the Fed starts easing in December 2027, taking gold to $4,650 by Dec27.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 weigh on private investor positioning through early 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A third 25bp Fed hike in March 2027 is already in the base case. A further hawkish shift beyond it would push toward the downside price scenario.

tension_points.bull_case: Electrification, data center and AI demand against constrained mine supply and low ex-US stocks lift copper to $15,600 by Dec27.
tension_points.bear_case: A reduction in US tariff ambiguity and a lackluster recovery in AI-related investor length present near-term downside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reduction in US tariff ambiguity, or a failure of AI-related investor length to recover.
